Technology stocks were falling Friday afternoon, with shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 losing 1.5% while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was declining 1.4%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Mellanox Technologies ( MLNX ) soared Friday, soared Friday with a nearly 18% advance, following a CNBC report that said the company hired an investment bank to assist with exploring a potential sale.
In other sector news:
(+) National Instruments ( NATI ) climbed almost 17% on Friday after Deutsche Bank raised its investment recommendation for the automation and measurement software firm to buy from hold and also increased its price target for the company's stock by $5 to $50 a share. The upgrade follows National Instruments late Thursday reporting non-GAAP Q3 net income of $0.45 per share on $346.1 million in revenue, exceeding the Capital IQ consensus for earnings and revenue.
(+) Intel ( INTC ) was more than 3% higher in afternoon trading, easing from earlier higher levels, after the chip-making giant beat analyst Q3 estimates on both the top and bottom lines.
(-) Alphabet ( GOOG ) at one point slid almost 6% lower on Friday after missing analyst estimates with its Q3 revenue. Total revenue surged year-over-year to $33.74 billion but still lagged the Capital IQ consensus. The internet conglomerate earned $13.06 per share during the three months ended Sept. 30, improving on a $9.57 per share profit last year and beating the Street view of $10.41 a share.
